_meta.purpose: The supplier-facing catalogue. Every component carries cost, carbon by LCA module, and — critically — a reversibility score that determines how much of it survives a change of use. This is where furniture and component suppliers plug in.

lca_modules.A1A3: Product stage — raw material supply, transport, manufacturing
lca_modules.A5: Installation, including waste of the product itself
lca_modules.B4: Replacement over the study period — derived from service_life, not stored
lca_modules.D: Benefits beyond the system boundary — reuse/recycling credit. Reported SEPARATELY and never netted into the headline, per EN 15978.

_meta.provenance_policy: Every cost and carbon value below is PLACEHOLDER: an order-of-magnitude working figure for Swedish 2026 conditions, used to develop and test the engine. Replace with supplier EPDs (EN 15804+A2) and priced quotations before any published result. engine/cli.py doctor reports placeholder share on every run.
_meta.supplier_onboarding: A supplier submits one JSON object per product using this schema. The three fields they most often cannot supply are reversibility, recovery_rate and C1C4 — which is precisely why those fields exist here. Asking for them changes the conversation.

components.name: Cast in-situ concrete wall, 200 mm
components.notes: The benchmark for irreversibility. Included so the engine can price the counterfactual: what a change of use costs when the space plan was built as structure.

components.name: Steel stud partition, 2×12.5 gypsum both sides, 95 mm, taped and painted
components.notes: The default. Cheap to build, almost total loss on removal — recovery_rate 0.05 because taped-and-skimmed board cannot be lifted intact. Every scenario comparison in this lab is essentially a case against this line item.

components.name: Demountable solid partition, 100 mm, factory-finished panels
components.notes: Roughly 1.8× the first cost of stud-and-board, and it wins on the SECOND fit-out. The engine exists to show where that crossover sits for a given scenario sequence — that is the whole argument, and it is quantifiable.

components.name: Demountable single-glazed partition, 100 mm
components.notes: Borrows daylight into deep plan — directly relieves the max_plan_depth_from_facade constraint that blocks residential conversion of office shells. Worth modelling as a daylight strategy, not just a partition.

components.name: Movable acoustic operable wall, top-hung, Rw 45

structural_demand.note: Top-hung tracks impose a line load on the slab or a transfer beam above. In reuse this is a STRUCTURE-layer check triggered by a SPACE_PLAN-layer choice — cheap to specify, expensive to discover late.

components.notes: Reconfiguration is measured in hours and near-zero carbon, but first cost is high and it needs annual maintenance. The honest trade-off: it converts capital carbon into operational flexibility.

components.name: Heavy acoustic curtain on ceiling track
components.notes: Very low Rw — visual and absorptive separation only, not acoustic privacy. Included because it is the cheapest, fastest, lowest-carbon subdivision available, and the engine should be able to show honestly where it is sufficient and where it is not.

components.name: Linoleum sheet flooring, 2.5 mm, adhered
components.notes: Low embodied carbon, zero recovery. A good reminder that low-carbon and reversible are different properties and must be scored separately.

components.name: Carpet tile, loose-laid with tackifier
components.notes: Higher embodied carbon than linoleum but fully recoverable and individually replaceable — the maintenance-carbon profile over 50 years may invert the ranking. The engine should decide this, not intuition.

components.name: Raised access floor, 150 mm void, steel/chipboard
components.notes: An ENABLE-layer investment: it buys servicing freedom for every future fit-out, at the price of 150 mm of floor-to-ceiling height. In a shell with tight floor-to-floor that trade is often unaffordable — which is exactly the kind of coupled decision the lab should expose.

components.name: Suspended mineral fibre tile ceiling on exposed grid
components.notes: Demountable, but tiles break on removal — hence recovery 0.55 against reversibility 0.90. Keeping those two numbers distinct is what stops the model flattering circular-design claims.

components.name: Suspended acoustic baffles / islands, free-hanging
components.notes: Resolves the exposed-thermal-mass vs acoustics conflict: partial coverage keeps most of the slab exposed for night cooling while meeting reverberation targets. Worth modelling as the default acoustic strategy in any low-operational-carbon scenario.

components.name: Folding table 1800×800, stackable
components.notes: stored_footprint_m2 is the field that lets the engine calculate the storage area a reconfigurable programme actually needs. Flexibility has a floor area, and this is how it gets counted.

components.name: Stacking chair
components.notes: Reused across every scenario at zero transformation carbon. In the engine's ledger these are the components that make a programme cheap to change — the fast layer doing its job.

components.name: Mobile storage / room-divider unit on castors
components.notes: Furniture doing the work of a wall. Where the brief needs territory rather than acoustic privacy, this substitutes for a partition at zero transformation cost — the highest-leverage move available in the fast layer.

components.name: Decentralised ventilation unit with heat recovery, per zone
components.notes: Decentralised units let ventilation capacity follow the programme zone by zone instead of requiring a whole-building plant replacement when one floor changes use. Higher unit carbon, radically better adaptability — a central thesis of this lab and a case the engine can now test rather than assert.

components.name: Central AHU with ducted distribution, per m² served
components.notes: Included so conventional and adaptable fit-outs can be compared on equal scope — otherwise the adaptable option carries a ventilation system its rival does not, and loses on a technicality. The ductwork, not the plant, holds most of the carbon here, which is why the decentralised alternative comes out lighter despite higher per-unit figures. Reconfiguring ducts when the space plan changes is also where a central system quietly taxes every future change of use.

components.name: New drainage stack through existing slabs, per floor

structural_demand.note: Coring through post-tensioned slabs may be prohibited outright. This is a hard IMPLEMENT-stage blocker, not a cost line — if the shell is PT, wet-room-intensive programmes may simply be unavailable away from existing stacks.

components.notes: Usually the single most decisive cost in converting office shells to any residential or care programme. Position of existing stacks effectively pre-selects which uses are affordable.

components.name: Replacement window, triple glazed, openable sash, in existing opening
components.notes: Replaces the 1985 fixed double glazing (U 2.8). Cuts heating demand and makes natural purge ventilation possible, which is what keeps a free-running dwelling out of overheating. Unit is m² of glazing.

components.name: Spandrel lowered from 900 to 600 mm, new glazing below transom
components.notes: Cutting down the precast spandrel to give a seated view (eye height ~1180 mm). A SKIN-layer intervention: expensive, irreversible, and the only way a wheelchair user or a care resident in bed sees out. Unit is m² of new glazing added below the old sill.
